R3.allowed_thresholds_reason: ADDED 2026-09-18 (claim gate R5, the largest single cluster on this property). The 20% CFM(50) air-sealing and 20% CFM(25) duct-sealing blower-door figures are QUALIFYING CONDITIONS, not amounts: they say what a homeowner must MEASURE to be eligible, and say nothing whatever about what any program pays. _shared_components.py carves them out of the 2026-09-09 no-rebate-figure ruling BY NAME, in the same breath as the R-value thresholds and the 75%/50% structure percentages: 'WHAT IS NOT COVERED BY THIS BAN ... the 20% CFM(50) and 20% CFM(25) blower-door thresholds'. The config had allowed_structure_percentages populated and allowed_thresholds EMPTY, so half of one Director ruling was wired and the other half was not -- which is why ~30 sentences stating a sanctioned threshold were adjudicated as uncited statistics. This registers the ruling that already exists; it does not create an exemption. Both spellings are listed because the prose uses '20 percent' as well as '20%', and the threshold_context_markers below still have to fire for either to clear.
R3.threshold_context_markers_reason: RESTATES common.json's nine markers verbatim and appends five. Restated because _deep_merge REPLACES lists rather than unioning them, so a partial list here would silently DROP the nine shared markers for GCI -- a config edit that reads as additive and is actually subtractive. The five additions are the vocabulary GCI's prose actually uses around the blower-door threshold; 'CFM' alone does not fire on sentences written as 'a 20% reduction in leakage'. PROPERTY-LOCAL: this key lives in gci.json, so common.json is untouched and DCI and LGM are unaffected.

R5.recognised_publishers_reason: RESTATES common.json's list VERBATIM and appends three census identifiers. Restated because _deep_merge REPLACES lists rather than unioning them, so a partial list here would silently drop every shared publisher for GCI. The additions close a real gap: this property attributes its housing-age figures to '(Census Bureau American Community Survey 5-year estimates)' -- the wording already used across its town pages -- and no census identifier was in recognised_publishers, so a correctly-cited census figure adjudicated as UNCITED. R5.computed_output_markers_reason: RESTATES common.json's eight markers VERBATIM and appends two. Restated because _deep_merge REPLACES lists rather than unioning them, so a partial list here would silently drop the eight shared markers for GCI. The two additions are Ruling 4 (visitor arithmetic) applied to arithmetic the page SHOWS ITS WORKING FOR, which is the same principle: (1) 'scales with 1/R' governs 'Conductive loss through a ceiling scales with 1/R, so going from R-15 to R-49 removes roughly 69% of it' -- the sentence states the method and both inputs, so a reader can check 1-15/49 themselves; the 69% is derived in front of them, not asserted about the world. (2) 'modeled here at' governs 'The ceiling's share of total household heat loss is modeled here at 8.5% to 23.5%' -- 'modeled HERE' explicitly labels the span as this calculator's own assumption rather than a published finding, and the same sentence names ENERGY STAR's Climate Zone 5 figure as the centre it was built around. Neither marker can clear a figure about a REBATE: both are anchored on method vocabulary that no rebate sentence on this property uses.

quotation_allowlist.text: The EPA's mold-sampling guidance states plainly
quotation_allowlist.why: VERIFIED VERBATIM, WITH A PROVENANCE RECORD IN THE REPO. attic-mold-greeley.html quotes 'In most cases, if visible mold growth is present, sampling is unnecessary.' R1 half B is a STRING LIST, not a claim test: it fires on a quote glyph near an attribution verb and has no way to see that a prose quotation is backed. The backing exists: _shared_components.py CITED_SOURCES['EPA_MOLD_TESTING_NOT_REQUIRED'], quote=True with a complete {retrieved, artifact, extraction, verbatim_line} record, re-fetched 2026-09-01 and confirmed byte-for-byte. Re-verified independently 2026-09-18 across 54 EPA documents (all HTTP 200): the sentence appears verbatim on https://www.epa.gov/mold/samplingtesting-mold-necessary as the FIRST sentence of the answer, and again in 'A Brief Guide to Mold, Moisture and Your Home' and Chapter 3 of the Schools and Commercial Buildings guide. The quotation is exact and the surrounding prose does not narrow or strengthen it.

quotation_allowlist.text: Usually not, and the EPA says so directly

quotation_allowlist.text: does not have a certification program for mold inspectors or mold remediation firms
quotation_allowlist.why: VERIFIED VERBATIM 2026-09-18, and newly backed. The quoted span is a byte-exact substring of EPA's sentence 'EPA does not have a certification program for mold inspectors or mold remediation firms.' on https://www.epa.gov/mold/who-can-test-my-home-or-clean-fix-and-remediate-my-home-mold (EPA page last updated 2026-01-14). Swept 54 EPA mold documents, every one HTTP 200; the sentence occurs EXACTLY ONCE across all of them. A registry entry was ADDED for it in the same pass -- CITED_SOURCES['EPA_MOLD_NO_CERTIFICATION'], quote=True with a complete provenance record -- because the page had been publishing this quotation with nothing behind it. QUALIFICATION KEPT ON RECORD rather than smoothed away: the page says EPA 'states directly', and this is the answer to one FAQ, not a headline EPA position. The words are EPA's and unaltered; the implied prominence is the site's. Do not strengthen that wording.

A QUOTED TERM, NOT AN ATTRIBUTED PROPOSITION. The sentence reads: The agency's own term is 'mycotoxins,' the potentially toxic substances some molds can produce. Half B cannot distinguish a scare-quoted or named NOUN from a quoted CLAIM, so a single word in quotation marks trips the same wire as a fabricated sentence. The term is genuinely EPA's: verified 2026-09-18 on https://www.epa.gov/mold/can-mold-cause-health-problems -- 'Molds produce allergens (substances that can cause allergic reactions), irritants, and in some cases, potentially toxic substances (mycotoxins).' Note EPA hedges with 'in some cases, potentially toxic', and this page's gloss preserves that hedge ('potentially toxic substances some molds can produce') rather than asserting harm.

quotation_allowlist.text: HPS is fatal in nearly 4 in 10 people who are infected
quotation_allowlist.why: VERIFIED VERBATIM 2026-09-18 AND CORRECTED IN THE SAME PASS -- this string is the CORRECTED text, and it is quotable precisely because it was fixed. The page previously printed CDC's phrase 'nearly 4 in 10' inside quotation marks with the site's OWN denominator substituted around it ('for people who develop HPS'), while CDC's sentence reads 'HPS is fatal in nearly 4 in 10 people who are INFECTED.' Different denominators; CDC uses a third, narrower one elsewhere ('Thirty-eight percent of people who develop respiratory symptoms may die from the disease'), so a ~38% rate cannot be true of all three. The site's wording matched none of them. Source: CDC 'Clinician Brief: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS)', https://www.cdc.gov/hantavirus/hcp/clinical-overview/hps.html, page dated 2026-05-08, retrieved via three Wayback raw-HTML reads because CDC returns 403 to curl -- so the quoted string is greppable bytes, not a summarizer's reconstruction. The page's source LABEL was corrected too: the PARENT /clinical-overview/ page carries no fatality figure at all. Registry entry: CITED_SOURCES['CDC_HPS_CLINICAL_OVERVIEW'].

FIRST-PARTY SCARE QUOTES -- NOTHING IS ATTRIBUTED TO ANYONE. about.html reads: The guidance here says 'not yet' as often as it says 'yes,' because the referral is only worth making when the work is worth doing. The grammatical subject is 'The guidance here' -- this site's own editorial stance -- and the quoted spans are two ordinary words used as examples of what the site itself tells people. No external source is named, so there is no source to have fabricated a quotation from. R1 half B fires on a quote glyph within 40 characters of an attribution verb, and 'says' is on that verb list; it has no way to check WHO is doing the saying. THIS ENTRY IS A STOPGAP, NOT THE CAUSE FIX. The real fix is requiring a NAMED PUBLISHER before half B's 'says' trigger fires, which another row is applying to common.json and which this row deliberately did NOT duplicate to avoid a collision. WHEN THAT LANDS, DELETE THIS ENTRY AND RE-MEASURE -- it should become redundant, and leaving a redundant allowlist entry in place is how a real future defect gets cleared by accident.
